Kotlin is a modern, statically typed, cross-platform programming language developed by JetBrains (the creators of IntelliJ IDEA and Android Studio) and first released in 2011. It was officially launched as an open-source project in 2012, designed to address common pain points found in traditional Java development—such as verbose syntax, boilerplate code, and frequent null pointer exceptions—while maintaining full compatibility with existing Java frameworks and libraries.
In 2017, Google announced Kotlin as an officially supported language for Android app development, and by 2019, Google made Kotlin the preferred language for Android developers.
